findings.evidence: docs/validation/host-selection.json records observation_payload.bundle_manifest_sha256 = f900ccdbf1cf40df66d6c6851015631af5b5da152da15eec60db7653df07ed6d, which test/real-host/host-selection.test.ts:570-572 computes as sha256 of dist/manifest.json at run time. The implementation output's own entry for dist/manifest.json carries payload_digest f58de93a06d94dcd33238c753425cd1c4eca9fdd224f633e90ce25d3ce8ad07a, and impl-notes records the post-merge regeneration as "release-offline green after the dist regen (manifest f58de93a…)" while the earlier flattening measurement is recorded against "manifest digest f900ccdb…". The post-merge verification list in impl-notes contains typecheck, schema generation/check, contracts, mcp-runtime, full vitest (with the opt-in real-host groups skipped) and release-offline — the ARCHFLOW_REAL_HOSTS run is not among them, and the always-on digest-contract test at test/real-host/host-selection.test.ts:490-512 checks the artifact's internal self-consistency only, never bundle_manifest_sha256 against the current dist, so nothing fails on the drift.
findings.suggested_resolution: Either re-run `ARCHFLOW_REAL_HOSTS=1 npx vitest run test/real-host/host-selection.test.ts` against the final tracked dist so the recorded bundle_manifest_sha256 matches the shipped bytes, or state explicitly in the impl notes and in the artifact that the evidence was taken against the pre-merge bundle and name the automated post-merge pins (mcp-advertised-schema, contract agreement) relied on for the final catalogue; optionally add an assertion that bundle_manifest_sha256 equals the current dist/manifest.json digest so future drift is caught.
findings.summary: The recorded real-host evidence required by success criterion 8 is digest-bound to a bundle that is no longer the shipped tracked dist, and it was not re-recorded after the main merge and dist regeneration.

findings.evidence: docs/validation/real-host-journeys.md:260-263 tells the operator to "Record that the decision-bearing `archflow_gate` or `archflow_waiver` call returns in the same invocation" and that "after approval the nonhuman `archflow-local commit` action must run without a second confirmation"; line 473 instructs a recovery invocation to "call archflow_state once ... then run archflow-local status --task val12-manual". All four names are retired by this change (src/contracts/tool-names.ts:18, src/mcp/server.ts:150, and the LOCAL_COMMANDS list pinned at test/contracts/retired-surface.test.ts:103-111). The file was edited in this phase to append the host-selection journey (section at line 497), but a grep for "superseded|retired|historical" returns no annotation on the older VAL-08/VAL-09/VAL-12 steps, and the document's opening still reads as an active procedure ("Run all three ...", lines 3-6).
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a short supersession note to the affected VAL sections (as was done for docs/validation/client-interface-audit.md's status line) marking those steps as point-in-time evidence against the retired four-tool surface, or restate the decision/commit observation steps on the semantic `archflow_status`/`archflow_apply` surface.
findings.summary: The operator runbook this phase edited still instructs observing the now-retired `archflow_gate`, `archflow_waiver`, `archflow_state`, and `archflow-local commit` surfaces, with no supersession annotation.
